title: Riksarkivet key-box and Oxenstierna ciphers, 8 records (Bremen 1631, R4282, R4306 and Rusdorff 1625 read or partly read and removed)
correspondents: unknown → Camerarius?, Amsterdam; Rusdorff → Oxenstierna; Swedish agent → Oxenstierna
status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only.
why: One remaining key-box ciphertext that resisted a first attack, and Oxenstierna correspondence of 1628 and 1633 with a key collection that may hold their keys.

title: Willem Frederik Roell (1767-1829), minister of Foreign Affairs (Amsterdam) to Frederik Gijsbertvan Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820), 2 ciphertexts
correspondents: Willem Frederik Roell (1767-1829), minister of Foreign Affairs → Frederik Gijsbertvan Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820)
shelfmark: NA The Hague, legatie Turkije, inv.nr. 804 (2 items)
status: DECODE R1469-R1470 viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/roell1809/). 13 pages of code throughout, unaddressed and unsigned; no decipherment on the scans. 2,585 groups (931 distinct) to about 3,300, heavily homophonic (no group above ~1%), not alphabetical. Not the 1788-93 Dedem code (overlap at chance), nor the Spaen 1808 or Fagel 1804 codes. No DECODE key; Roell's papers (NA 2.21.008.78) list letters from Dedem and from S. F. Croiset 1808-09 but no codebook. Not breakable without the key or a crib.
why: Ciphered despatches of Willem Frederik Roell (1767-1829), minister of Foreign Affairs to Frederik Gijsbertvan Dedem tot de Gelder (1743-1820), 9 Feb 1809; what the cipher hides is not known.

title: Transylvanian cipher letters, Keresdi Bethlen and Kemény collections
shelfmark: Romanian National Archives, Cluj: Keresdi Bethlen 14–15, Kemény XIX
status: Checked 22 Sept 2026: DECODE R4933-R4942 are N/A with no decryption attached, and no published reading was found; the collection is at the Romanian National Archives in Cluj, not Sibiu. Split by system 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry). Narrowed 23 Oct 2026: R4937, R4940 and R4942 read with the Bethlen family key recovered ciphertext-only, and R4939 broken ciphertext-only in its own key and read (targets/transylvania1645/, transylvania1645.html); they leave the catalogue. Still open: R4936 (decoded with the family key, not read: g/q look-alikes the 1,704-px scan cannot separate), R4938 (three short spans decoded, one word unread), R4941 (a different substitution, targets/r4941/) and the Kemény XIX records R4933-R4935 (targets/kemeny1628/).
why: Transylvania under George I Rákóczi, around the peace of Linz (1645).

title: Magnus Stenbock (prisoner in Copenhagen) ↔ Peter Malmberg: cipher correspondence; key in Malmberg's papers
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Peter Malmbergs (Palmcreutz) arkiv, SE/RA/720725/~/E 4698 (key); letters in Ericsbergsarkivets autografsamling
folio_note: Key: "chiffernyckel mellan Magnus Stenbock och Malmberg för brevväxling under Stenbocks fångenskap"; letters: Ericsbergsarkivet autograph collection (not yet located item-level).
status: Catalogue (E 4698): key for the captivity correspondence; "brev från denna brevväxling finns i Ericsbergsarkivets autografsamling". DECODE R4101 (KB, Stenbock autografsamling 1713) is a different, decrypted item. Not in the repo. The 24 Oct Riksarkivet sweep found the key only in E 4698; the letters themselves are in the Ericsberg autograph collection. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): not blocked: Erlund's 1732 manuscript in the Riksarkivet (SE/RA/760004/42, IIIF R0000422, public domain) holds the key (Lit. F) and interlinear decipherments of the intercepted letters, the escape contract included. Stenbock's enciphered petition to Charles XII (pp. 697-707) is a different code, only partly glossed by Erlund; Dudout has rebuilt about a third of its values with certainty. See targets/stenbock1713/.
why: Stenbock's secret letters from Danish captivity (escape plans led to his close confinement in 1714); key and letters both survive.
